key_insight: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks embedded in finite element model updating learn hyperelastic behavior from heterogeneous experiments and yield compact, closed-form strain energies.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce reliance on predefined constitutive laws and multiple homogeneous tests while producing interpretable material models for finite element analysis.
method: Embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network in finite element model updating.
Fit measured kinematic fields and reaction forces.
Apply pruning and symbolic regression to extract closed-form energies satisfying constitutive requirements.
evidence_signal: Rubber tests showed median displacement errors of 1–2% and transfer to a withheld hole pattern; silicone predictions matched a measured profile and force within a few percent, while an anisotropic model predicted an inflated aortic specimen’s 3D shape.
watch_item: Transfer to a withheld geometry is demonstrated, but generalization beyond the measured loading conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
